key_insight: VibeTraining-Bench evaluates whether research agents can improve target agent systems by jointly refining training data, trainers, and inference harnesses.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark tests coordinated training-and-inference optimization under fixed resource budgets rather than isolated component tuning.
method: Start from identical initial systems within each task and use validation feedback to guide iterative improvements.
Co-design data, trainers, and inference harnesses, then submit a final system for held-out testing.
Enforce test-data isolation, separate research and grading containers, and research-agent network restrictions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that GPT-6-Astra raises SWE-bench Verified performance from 32.9% to 53.7%, versus 55.4% for a human-developed instruct model; tasks also cover terminal operation, multi-turn tool use, and mathematical reasoning.
watch_item: The abstract leaves mathematical-reasoning-specific gains unquantified and notes that cumulative improvement through iterative co-design remains limited.
paper_title: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement
